TestClusteringKeyFilter::test_check_cons.description: Single node, cache off, compaction disabled. Rows key1/a and key2/b each flushed to own sstable; then key1/c (memtable) + partition delete of key2 flushed together, so key2's tombstone lives in an sstable whose ck range is [c,c]. SELECT p1 IN (key1,key2) AND c1 in [a,b] must return only key1/a, i.e. the CK filter must not drop the sstable holding key2's partition tombstone.

origin.summary: Raphael Carvalho: dtest for correctness of clustering range filter (sstable min/max clustering metadata), added alongside scylla 8d03ccd604 'sstables: optimize reads with clustering filter'; row cache disabled so reads hit sstables.

TestClusteringKeyFilter::test_check_cons.reason: Mostly unique end-to-end check that a partition tombstone in an sstable outside the queried ck range still shadows older rows under TWCS CK filtering; partial overlap with test_time_window_clustering_slicing and cqlpy test_clustering_filtering*. Cheap and easily portable to cqlpy (flush + BYPASS CACHE + no_autocompaction_context). Note: name says 'row tombstone' but it is a partition delete (remove_row, :244). Note: helper check_number_of_rows assert message is str(len(result)) (always '1'), not the actual count (clustering_key_filter_test.py:236). Note: no test checks the filter was actually exercised (e.g. cf_stats clustering_filter_count / sstables_checked_by_clustering_filter metrics), only result correctness.
